shortDescription: An End-only conduit upgrade: activates in the End, grants Conduit Power (and thus air) with a Glowstone/End Stone/End Stone Bricks/Sea Lantern frame, no water needed.
oneLiner: A craftable violet conduit for the End: surround it with 16 Glowstone, End Stone, End Stone Bricks or Sea Lanterns - no water needed - and it grants Conduit Power on dry End ground, which (with the End Oxygen module enabled) means you can breathe there indefinitely.
events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddReloadListenerEvent (NeoForge game bus; the module instance subscribes itself via NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) in onInitialize, handler EndConduitModule#onAddReloadListener at EndConduitModule.java:153-159, returns early unless isModuleEnabled(); it adds a PreparableReloadListener that injects the crafting recipe on the game executor)
net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers (mod bus, Dist.CLIENT, EndConduitClientSetup#onRegisterRenderers - binds EndConduitBER to the block entity type)

net.neoforged.neoforge.client.extensions.common.RegisterClientExtensionsEvent (mod bus, Dist.CLIENT, EndConduitClientSetup#onRegisterClientExtensions - EndConduitItemRenderer as the item's custom renderer)
recipes: Shaped, injected in code at every datapack reload (AddReloadListenerEvent -> EndConduitRecipeReloadListener -> EndConduitModule#applyEndConduitRecipe, which rebuilds the recipe map and calls RecipeManager.replaceRecipes; gated on isModuleEnabled() when the event fires); recipe id vanillaplusadditions:end_conduit, CraftingBookCategory.MISC - pattern FEF / ECE / FEF with F = minecraft:chorus_fruit (4 corners), E = minecraft:ender_eye (4 edges), C = minecraft:conduit (centre) -> 1x vanillaplusadditions:end_conduit.

configKeys.effect: Minimum frame-block count (Glowstone / End Stone / End Stone Bricks / Sea Lantern) required to activate the End Conduit. Vanilla conduit uses 16; 42 is the maximum the ring geometry can hold. Read live on both sides, so it also decides what the client renders as active.

Conduit Power radius = (actual frame count / 7 * 16) / this divisor, floored at 1 block (all integer division). 1 (default) = full vanilla Conduit Power radius: 32 blocks at a 16-block frame, 96 at a full 42-block frame. The module additionally clamps the value with Math.max(1, ...).

notes:
DOCS STATUS
- There is NO docs/modules/end_conduit.md (verified with ls docs/modules/). The only prose today is README.md:98-99 ("#### :milky_way: End Conduit") plus the class javadocs in EndConduitModule.java:44-54, EndConduitBlock.java:25-30 and EndConduitBlockEntity.java:24-39. A doc writer starts from zero here.

WHAT CONTRADICTS THE README / JAVADOC
- README says it "renders like a vanilla conduit"; EndConduitModule's javadoc says "rendered identically to the vanilla conduit (same texture + animation, via a copied renderer)". That is outdated. Since 1971b8a (v1.0.0-beta.47) block and item use OUR OWN violet + endstone-gold tinted sprites under textures/block/end_conduit/ (base, cage, wind, wind_vertical, open_eye, closed_eye, with .mcmeta animations on both wind sprites, bound in EndConduitTextures), and since 2308dd3 (v1.0.0-beta.53) the nautilus particle is a tinted copy too (assets/vanillaplusadditions/particles/end_nautilus.json -> textures/particle/end_nautilus.png). It looks like a RECOLOURED conduit, not an identical one. Only the MODEL GEOMETRY is vanilla: EndConduitBER bakes ModelLayers.CONDUIT_EYE/WIND/SHELL/CAGE, no new model layer is registered.
- Break/step particle mismatch (still true): models/block/end_conduit.json is nothing but {"textures": {"particle": "minecraft:block/sea_lantern"}} (the block itself renders as RenderShape.ENTITYBLOCK_ANIMATED, so the model exists only to carry that particle texture), while models/item/end_conduit.json uses parent builtin/entity with particle vanillaplusadditions:block/end_conduit/base. Breaking the block throws sea-lantern-white particles, not tinted ones.

THE AIR PART IS NOT THIS MODULE
- The End Conduit only grants MobEffects.CONDUIT_POWER. Breathing in the End comes from the separate end_oxygen module: EndOxygenModule.java:74 checks getConfig().conduitPowerGrantsAir() && player.hasEffect(MobEffects.CONDUIT_POWER); that key is "conduit_power_grants_air", default true (EndOxygenConfig.java:52-55). Disable end_oxygen, or set that key false, and the End Conduit gives Conduit Power only. This coupling is the module's whole selling point and lives in another module's config.

ACTIVATION / EFFECT MECHANICS (EndConduitBlockEntity)
- Frame ring geometry is byte-for-byte the vanilla conduit ring (the -2..2 loop, EndConduitBlockEntity.java:118-135). Counted out, that ring has exactly 42 positions - which is why 42 is both the config's upper bound for min_frames and the hardcoded MIN_HUNT_SIZE. Only the accepted blocks differ: GLOWSTONE, END_STONE, END_STONE_BRICKS, SEA_LANTERN (VALID_FRAME, lines 43-45). No prismarine.
- No water requirement at all - vanilla's inner 3x3x3 water check is simply absent, and applyEffects has no water/rain gate.
- Activation also requires level.dimension() == Level.END AND EndConduitModule.isModuleActive() (isEnabledHere, lines 101-104). Outside the End it never lights up.
- Shape/activation is only recomputed when gameTime % 40 == 0 -> up to 2 s delay after finishing the frame or after a chunk load. Nothing is persisted to NBT (the BE overrides no saveAdditional/loadAdditional), so state is always rebuilt from the world.
- Conduit Power is applied every 40 ticks with duration 260 ticks, amplifier 0, ambient = true, visible = true (line 167) - so it survives the 2 s gap comfortably.
- Sounds mirror vanilla: SoundEvents.CONDUIT_ACTIVATE / CONDUIT_DEACTIVATE on every state change, CONDUIT_AMBIENT every 80 game ticks while active, CONDUIT_AMBIENT_SHORT at a random 60-100 tick cadence (serverTick, lines 79-98). Nautilus particles are spawned client-side only (animationTick, lines 172-187, roughly 1/50 per frame block per tick).
- applyEffects builds an AABB inflated by radius and then expandTowards(0, level.getHeight(), 0), but the per-player check is pos.closerThan(player.blockPosition(), radius). The vertical expansion therefore only widens the candidate list; the granted area stays a sphere. This mirrors vanilla exactly - mention it only if someone wonders about the odd-looking box.

RADIUS MATH GOTCHA
- EndConduitModule.effectRadius(frames) = Math.max(1, frames / 7 * 16 / divisor), all integer division, floors at every step. Note it takes the ACTUAL frame count (positions.size()), not min_frames. With a 16-block frame and divisor 1: 16/7 = 2 -> 2*16 = 32 blocks; a full 42-block frame gives 42/7*16 = 96. Same table as a vanilla conduit.
- If min_frames is lowered below 7 and the player really builds fewer than 7 frame blocks, the conduit activates but frames/7 == 0 and the radius collapses to the Math.max(1, ...) floor of 1 block. Not documented anywhere.
- divisor is additionally guarded with Math.max(1, ...) in EndConduitModule.effectRadius, so a corrupt 0 cannot divide by zero.

COSMETIC-ONLY "HUNTING" FLAG
- MIN_HUNT_SIZE = 42 is hardcoded (line 42). isHunting is set purely from positions.size() >= 42 (updateHunting, lines 106-108) and is used for exactly one thing: EndConduitBER draws OPEN_EYE instead of CLOSED_EYE (EndConduitBER.java:97-100). The End Conduit NEVER attacks mobs - there is no attack code at all.
- Consequence of the hardcoding: min_frames is configurable up to 42, so at min_frames = 42 the eye opens the moment it activates; with anything lower the eye stays shut until the frame really reaches 42 blocks.
- The separate conduit_attack_range module only mixes into vanilla's ConduitBlockEntity (mixin/conduit_attack_range/ConduitBlockEntityMixin, vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json:16, build.gradle:411-412). It does NOT touch the End Conduit - these two modules are unrelated despite the similar names.

DISABLING THE MODULE (corrected - it is NOT a data-loss switch)
- In the bundle jar, onInitialize() runs for EVERY registered module no matter what the toml says: VanillaPlusAdditions.java:114 calls ModuleManager.initializeModules BEFORE the config spec even exists (registerConfig at :131 is what first triggers ModulesConfig.buildConfig via getSpec()), so at that moment AbstractModuleConfig.isEnabled() finds its ModConfigSpec.BooleanValue still null and falls back to module.isEnabledByDefault() = true (Module.java:73, not overridden here). Therefore block, item, block entity type and particle type are ALWAYS registered, the creative-tab entry is always added, and the "End Conduit module initialized" line always appears in the log. Setting end_conduit.enabled = false does NOT unregister anything and does NOT turn placed End Conduits into unknown blocks.
- What disabling really does: isEnabledHere() fails, so the block never activates (no Conduit Power, no particles, closed-eye shell only), and onAddReloadListener returns early, so the crafting recipe is not injected on the next datapack reload. The block stays placeable, obtainable from the creative tab and still drops itself.
- Because AbstractModule.isModuleEnabled() resolves through ModuleManager.resolveModuleEnabled on every call, /vpa module enable|disable|status|clear (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:239-265) and edits to the toml take effect immediately for activation; the recipe follows on the next /reload.
- The earlier worry that EndConduitClientSetup (annotated @EventBusSubscriber(value = Dist.CLIENT, bus = MOD), so auto-discovered regardless of module state) would blow up on END_CONDUIT_BE.get() / END_NAUTILUS.get() / END_CONDUIT_ITEM.get() when the module is disabled does not apply to the bundle: registration always ran, so those holders are always bound.

THE STANDALONE JAR IS A DUD (biggest finding)
- build.gradle:422 declares the descriptor [ moduleId: 'end_conduit', displayName: 'Vanilla Plus: End Conduit' ] -> modId vpa_end_conduit, entrypointPkg end_conduit, no dataGlobs, no moduleDeps, no mixins. moduleJar_end_conduit therefore builds and CI publishes it (release.yml:49 `./gradlew moduleJars`, release.yml:88 attaches build/libs/modules/*.jar).
- BUT the jar task packs `${basePkg}/standalone/${entrypointPkg}/**` (build.gradle:642) and there is NO src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/standalone/end_conduit/ package - `git log --all -- .../standalone/end_conduit` is empty, it never existed. Of the standaloneModules entries only end_conduit and conduit_attack_range lack their @Mod entrypoint; every other module has one (pattern: standalone/<id>/<Name>Standalone.java calling StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot(new <Name>Module(), modEventBus, modContainer), e.g. EndOxygenStandalone.java).
- Provable consequence: without that entrypoint no EndConduitModule is ever constructed in the standalone jar, so onInitialize() never runs, the DeferredRegisters are never attached to a mod bus and nothing is registered - the jar ships no block, no item, no recipe. (Whether NeoForge additionally refuses to load a javafml mod file with no @Mod class, or whether the still-packed EndConduitClientSetup then crashes the client on unbound holders, cannot be decided from this repo.) hasStandaloneJar is kept true because the descriptor and the jar task exist, but the jar is not usable.

CLIENT/SERVER SPLIT AND A POSSIBLE DESYNC
- Both sides tick independently (clientTick / serverTick) and each recomputes activation itself; the javadoc states this is deliberate so no packet sync is needed. But both isEnabledHere() and the min_frames threshold are read from the module's own config on each side, and that config is a COMMON spec (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:131 registers ModConfig.Type.COMMON), i.e. a per-installation file that is not synced to clients. A client whose local config disables end_conduit or uses a different min_frames would render the conduit inactive (or active) while the server disagrees about the Conduit Power. Derived from the code, not tested in game.

BLOCK / ITEM PROPERTIES
- MapColor.COLOR_PURPLE, strength(3.0F, 3.0F), SoundType.METAL, lightLevel = 15 UNCONDITIONALLY (EndConduitModule.java:79) - it glows at full brightness even when inactive or outside the End - and noOcclusion. Hitbox is the vanilla conduit's 6x6x6 core (Block.box(5,5,5,11,11,11)). NOT waterloggable (deliberate: "the End has no water"). RenderShape.ENTITYBLOCK_ANIMATED, so all visuals come from EndConduitBER.
- Drops are code-side: getDrops() returns List.of(new ItemStack(this)) unconditionally (EndConduitBlock.java:72-75). It ignores Silk Touch, tool and explosion context - it always drops itself, including when blown up.
- The item is a plain BlockItem with a default Item.Properties (stack size 64, no rarity), added to the mod's main creative tab via VanillaPlusCreativeTabs.addToMainTab. Its inventory look comes from EndConduitItemRenderer (a BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer baking ModelLayers.CONDUIT_SHELL with the tinted base sprite), wired through IClientItemExtensions.getCustomRenderer().

LANG
- Only one key exists: block.vanillaplusadditions.end_conduit. The BlockItem inherits it, so there is no separate item key. Translated in en_us ("End Conduit"), de_de/de_at ("End-Aquisator"), cs_cz ("Endovy majak"), es_es ("Conducto del End"), fr_fr ("Conduit de l'End"). The particle type has no lang key (none needed).

MISC
- Registration sites: block end_conduit (EndConduitBlock, EndConduitModule.java:73-80), item end_conduit (plain BlockItem, :82-83), block entity type end_conduit (:85-87), particle type end_nautilus (:90-91); all four DeferredRegisters are attached to the mod bus in onInitialize (:138-142).
- No TODO/FIXME/HACK comments anywhere in the module directory.
- No mixins (absent from vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json and from the build.gradle descriptor), no data/ files, no dataGlobs, no JEI plugin, no shouldInitialize() gate, no ModList.isLoaded() anywhere - so no required and no optional mod dependencies.
- Besides block and item the module registers a block entity type "end_conduit" and a particle type "end_nautilus" (SimpleParticleType, overrideLimiter false, never shown to the player by name). Neither is an entity in the mob sense, hence entities = [].
- Version trail: the module landed in v1.0.0-beta.46 (d73a4b0, 2026-07-22) as a functional but vanilla-looking conduit; the tinted textures + 3D item renderer arrived in v1.0.0-beta.47 (1971b8a), the tinted particle in v1.0.0-beta.53 (2308dd3). Screenshots taken before beta.53 will look wrong. Those three commits are the module directory's complete history.
